correctness.rationale: The proof identifies every envy-free assignment through unique top choices on a selected triple, rigorously discards a house favored by two agents, proves a uniform conditional next-choice law for each possible unresolved history, and multiplies exact conditional survival factors. Monotonicity yields the first-hitting distribution; gamma product and summation yield tail and mean. Exhaustive independently implemented subset and deletion tests for every normalized profile through six houses agree, without treating a finite census as infinite proof.

value.rationale: An exact all-horizon first-zero-subsidy feasibility distribution is a natural service-level benchmark in sequential housing models, directly quantifying the number of arrivals necessary before subsidies can be avoided when complete terminal reassignment is allowed. It resolves an entire infinite family and a finite expected waiting horizon; this precision is not supplied by prior asymptotic high-probability results. The small fixed number of agents is the smallest case with nontrivial collision types and a full law, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
